en.title: Slow Horses: How Many More Seasons Can This Spy Thriller Run?
en.summary: Apple TV+ has made the British spy thriller its longest-running show with an eighth season renewal. As the series catches up to the books, fans wonder about its future.
en.body:
Ahead of its sixth season premiere, **Slow Horses** has secured an unprecedented renewal for an eighth season on Apple TV+. This move cements the critically acclaimed British spy thriller as the streamer's longest-running original series, a testament to its enduring appeal. Fans of Mick Herron's Slough House novels, and indeed the show itself, have reason to celebrate as the misadventures of Jackson Lamb and his band of disgraced MI5 agents continue to captivate audiences worldwide.

The latest renewal comes as season 8 is slated to adapt the events of Herron's most recent Slough House novel, *Clown Town*. This presents a fascinating crossroads for the series. Typically, *Slow Horses* has followed a yearly release schedule, with season 6 premiering in September 2026 and season 7 expected in 2027. If this pattern holds, season 8 could arrive as early as 2028. By adapting *Clown Town*, the Apple TV+ series will be current with Herron's published Slough House entries, raising questions about how the show will proceed thereafter.

## The Source Material Conundrum

Executive producer Douglas Urbanski has acknowledged the unique challenge of adapting a series that is still actively being written. "Most TV shows don’t have books, so we can figure this out," he stated, hinting at the creative flexibility the production team possesses. Mick Herron has a prolific track record, publishing nine novels and five novellas in the Slough House series since 2010. This prolific output suggests that a *Game of Thrones*-esque 'lack of source material' scenario, where the show outpaces the books, might be avoidable. However, the creative team will eventually face decisions: will they develop original storylines, collaborate closely with Herron on future plot points, pause production to await more books, or consider bringing the series to a close once the existing novels are adapted?

## What Fans Are Saying

Fans have expressed immense satisfaction with the show's longevity, particularly in an era where many beloved series face premature cancellations. The consistent quality and the unique blend of dark humor, espionage, and character-driven drama have garnered a dedicated global following. The renewal for season 8, especially with the prospect of adapting *Clown Town*, has fueled excitement. Many viewers appreciate that *Slow Horses* continues to deliver compelling narratives without resorting to cheap thrills or dry exposition, maintaining an enthusiastic yet credible voice that resonates with smart, passionate fans who consume content primarily on mobile devices.

## What's Next

With season 6 set to premiere in September 2026, and season 7 anticipated in 2027, the focus now shifts to the implications of the season 8 renewal. Audiences can expect the show to continue its annual release cadence for the foreseeable future. The key question remains how the creative team will navigate the adaptation of future seasons once the current book arc is completed.

The renewal made the British spy thriller series the longest-running show on the streamer, and fans seemed pretty happy. Why wouldn’t they be? While other great shows are getting canceled or wrapping up their stories, Slow Horses just keeps on running, and there doesn’t seem to be an end in sight. Yet season 8 could inspire some big behind-the-scenes decisions for those shepherding the TV version of Mick Herron’s bestselling book series onto the small screen, as it will adapt the events of his most recent Slough House entry, Clown Town . After season 8, the Apple TV series could be up to date with Herron’s beloved tales of hapless espionage, which may mean some changes ahead. Slow Horses typically releases a season every year, so season 8 could realistically arrive in 2028. Herron isn’t done writing Slough House books, but if he doesn’t release another one (or even two) in good time before then, the series will be faced with a few choices: keep going with the writing team’s own ideas à la Game of Thrones , consult with Herron about any firm or detailed ideas he has for future instalments, delay work on further seasons and wait for the author to create more books, or put an end to the show. Herron has churned out nine Slough House novels and five novellas since 2010, so we can’t imagine Slow Horses fans will be left dealing with a Winds of Winter -esque situation here, but a lack of source material is already something that the creators of the series have had to consider. “Most TV shows don’t have books, so we can figure this out,” executive producer Douglas Urbanski told THR . “And there’s another thing: Mick Herron hasn’t stopped writing. I can’t speak for Mick, but you never know, more books might be coming.” Indeed, Herron confirmed to the Radio Times last year that “There will be more to come. I haven’t decided how many yet but I’m enjoying myself and don’t plan to stop just yet.” Yet until any new books are released, season 8’s spin on Clown Town could mark the end of one particular creative road for those adapting Herron’s work. As many fans already know, the story features Jackson Lamb and Diana Taverner’s ageing spies (played by Gary Oldman and Kristin Scott Thomas, respectively) as they’re forced into a dramatic face-off after someone tries to blackmail the Park. Oldman recently revealed at the Edinburgh TV Festival that it’s a “struggle and a fight” to keep the cast together and “keep on top of the quality” of Slow Horses , but he also told TV Insider that Apple TV will ultimately decide whether to “keep it going or end it.” With Season 8’s renewal confirmed, it seems fans will have another two seasons of Slow Horses to look forward to after the current one wraps up.
